function: Joint design of BS beamforming, NOMA power allocation and IRS phase shifts to maximize the sum secrecy rate against external and internal eavesdroppers (p. 5).
system: BS with M=5 antennas, K=2 single-antenna users, one single-antenna eavesdropper, passive reflecting IRS with N=100 elements, NOMA downlink; frequency band not stated (pp. 3, 8).
method: Graph neural network (CO-GNN): MLP input layer, message-passing layers with mean and max pooling, fully connected output; unsupervised training, loss is negative sum secrecy rate, Adam (pp. 5-8).
data_channel: Own simulator: Rayleigh BS-user links, Rician IRS links, path-loss formulas of Table II, random user positions; 10,000 training samples; no public or measured data (pp. 3, 8).
test_conditions: Trained and tested on the same simulator; sweeps over transmit power, IRS elements and antennas with K=2; no testing on conditions unseen in training stated (pp. 8-10).
baselines: Non-learned: alternating optimization (WMMSE, Riemannian conjugate gradient, genetic algorithm). Learned: three GNN variants of CO-GNN (average power, random IRS, omni-beam); no earlier learned method (p. 8).
metrics: Sum secrecy rate (bps/Hz) versus transmit power, IRS elements and antennas; training loss convergence; CPU data-loading and running time; IRS array response plots (pp. 9-12).
complexity: Order O((3x3+L) d_MLP T_R) with L=8, d_MLP=512, versus AO order; measured CPU data-loading and running time, Fig. 12; no parameter or FLOP count (pp. 11-12).
q1_support: p. 3: "modeled by Rayleigh fading" (custom simulator with Rayleigh and Rician fading and own path-loss formulas; no 3GPP TR 38.901, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is mentioned)
q2_support: p. 10: "the influence of the number of transmit antennas M on the sum secrecy rate" (sweep with fixed K = 2; the paper never states that a model trained in one configuration is tested in another)
q3_support: p. 8: "we design a neural network model closely resembling CO-GNN" (the learned benchmarks are ablations of the proposed method; no earlier learned method or standard network such as a fully connected network or DQN is compared)
q4_support: p. 11: "the computational complexity is O"; p. 12: "the running time of different schemes in the CPU"
q5_support: p. 8: "10000 training samples being used to compute the gradients" (samples come from the paper's own simulator; no code or data link, no public dataset)
notes: PDF is the arXiv preprint 2506.05381v1; its title and authors match the Crossref record of this DOI (checked outside the PDF). Area 3: the GNN outputs the BS beamformer, NOMA power allocation and IRS phases; secrecy rate is the objective, and physical-layer security is not an excluded function. Learned benchmarks GNN & Average Power, GNN & Random IRS and GNN & Omni-beam each fix one variable of the proposed model, so they are ablations (q3 = 0); the alternating-optimization baseline is non-learned. Figs. 6-9 (p. 10) sweep N and M with K = 2; the output layers depend on M and N and retraining is not stated; p. 5 claims generalization to varying user counts but no experiment tests it. Paper inconsistencies: text says five benchmarks but lists four, Table II gives 1 message-passing layer but p. 6 says two, p. 9 mentions critic learning rate and action-value approximation although training uses gradient descent on the secrecy-rate loss.
